title: terraform: unify private state layout for GPU node pools, IAM & networking
author: Aditi Rao
description: Motivation: private deployments currently have fragmented Terraform state and module layouts across GPU node pools, IAM roles/policies, and VPC networking which makes cross-region restores, upgrades, and automated rollbacks fragile. This PR unifies the state layout and module boundaries to provide a single canonical state layout for Private (VPC/on-prem) installations, improves interoperability between node pool and networking modules, and makes IAM bindings explicit and stable. Summary of changes: consolidated state files into private/state/ (per-environment logical buckets), introduced a `gpu_node_pool` module with stable resource naming/suffixes, moved IAM role/policy definitions into `private/iam` with explicit module outputs, refactored VPC submodule to expose route table and subnet IDs for the node pool module, updated example workspaces and migration helpers, and added automated terratest coverage for multi-cluster upgrades. Migration notes: this change requires running the included migration helper (terraform state mv commands) or using the automated migration plan (scripts/migrate-state.sh) for existing customers; the PR includes idempotent helpers for minor drift. Rollout: feature is backward-compatible for new installs; existing installs must follow the migration_steps in this PR before applying the new module layout. Testing: unit-level terraform validate/lint, ci terratest runs against a small GPU cluster in the staging project, and manual upgrade tests performed for two customer-like environments. Related: linked Linear tasks ENG-1876, infra review INF-234.

release_notes: Unify Terraform state layout for Private deployments: introduces gpu_node_pool module, centralizes IAM and VPC outputs, adds migration helpers and terratest coverage. Existing installations must run provided migration helper before applying the updated layout.
migration_steps: 1) Checkout main and tag current state: ./scripts/backup-state.sh <env>
2) Run scripts/migrate-state.sh --preview to generate terraform state mv commands
3) Review and run generated terraform state mv commands in the appropriate workspace
4) Run terraform plan against examples/private-workspace to confirm no unexpected changes
5) Apply the new module layout once plan is clean
rollout_plan: Stage: run migration helper in staging workspace and validate application-level tests
Canary: pick one customer/private deployment, run migration during maintenance window
General rollout: roll through environments with monitoring enabled and rollback plan ready
